# `Q-2-2` — Mismatched Delimiter in Attribute Specifier

> Inside `{...}` attribute braces, the parser saw a delimiter
> that does not fit any of the expected attribute forms.

## What this means

A `{...}` attribute specifier on a span, link, image, or code
block accepts a fixed set of forms: an identifier `#name`, a class
`.classname`, a key-value pair `key=value`, or a language tag
inside a code block. When the parser sees a delimiter that
doesn't fit any of those — typically a stray bracket, brace, or
punctuation — it reports this error.

The expected continuations are: `}`, a language specifier, an
identifier (`#...`), a class (`.…`), or a key-value pair.

## Why this happens

The pattern often appears when nested brackets inside the
attribute block confuse the parser:

- **Nested unescaped brackets.** A `[` or `{` appearing inside
  attribute braces without an obvious meaning.
- **A typo in a key-value or class form.** A misplaced character
  that the attribute grammar does not recognize.

## How to fix

Re-examine the attribute braces at the location named in the
error. Each piece inside `{...}` should be one of the allowed
forms, separated by whitespace.

If a value really needs to contain special characters, quote it:

```markdown
[span]{key="value with [brackets]"}
```

## Example

```markdown
A bad [attribute]{[
```

The `[` inside the attribute braces is the unexpected delimiter.
